newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rally to new record, dollar climbs while gold steadies.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rally to new record, dollar climbs while gold steadies.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks powered to yet another record higher close on Tuesday, rising more than 100 points as investors expressed confidence about the outlook for the U.S. economy and second-quarter earnings.
The dollar hit a new 3-1/2-year high against the German mark after news of a rise in German unemployment, and gold prices rebounded from Monday's 12-year lows.

The 30-share Dow rose 103.82 points, or 1.32 percent, to 7,962.31, putting it within striking distance of the 8,000 mark. It was the 30th record this year for the world's most widely watched stock index, whose previous record of 7,895.81 came Thursday.

"Eight thousand is a foregone conclusion at this point," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We've been hemming and hawing just below 8,000, and the next time we make a move we'll probably blast right through."
Good profits from the first few companies to report only added to optimism as the earnings period gets into full swing, analysts said.
"Judging from the market, most people are looking for good numbers," said Peter Canelo, U.S. equity strategist at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter.
Broader market averages also hit new highs.

The Nasdaq composite index jumped 14.36 points to 1,485.10, its fourth consecutive record, on strong gains in technology stocks. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 6.55 points to 918.75 and the NYSE composite index rose 2.94 to 478.49, both records.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,680 to 1,122 on active volume of 525 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Meanwhile, the dollar hit a new 3-1/2-year high against the mark after Germany reported a rise of 11,000 in unemployment for June.
The dollar rose to 1.7612 marks from 1.7530 on Monday. It edged up to $1.6880 British pounds from $1.6903, and ended little changed vs. the Japanese yen at 112.85 yen, vs. 112.83 yen late Monday.
The 30-year Treasury fell 5/32, or $1.56 on a $1,000 bond, boosting its yield to 6.59 percent from 6.58 percent Monday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

Gold rebounded Tuesday as bargain-hunters resurfaced after the precious metal fell nearly $15 an ounce in three days. August gold closed up $2.00 at $321.20 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange, rallying from Monday's $319.00 an ounce, a level last seen in 1985.
Soybean prices soared Tuesday amid talk that a recent drop in prices had attracted overseas buying interest.

At the Chicago Board of Trade, soybeans for July delivery closed 35-1/4 cents a bushel higher at $7.68. The rally in soybeans aided corn prices, and July corn closed up 2-3/4 cents a bushel at $2.43-1/4.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 closed down 52.2 points, or 1.09 percent, at 4,758.5. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,853.89, up 148.72 points, or 0.75 percent.
